document_contracts.description: The document should contain the required top-level sections and expected subsection structure.
Each major section should follow the expected section structure, code-block requirements, and formatting rules defined by the template contract.
The document should keep section formatting, code-block style, and terminology consistent across all sections.

section_contracts.title: Purpose
checkitems: define the purpose of the current item design document
make the item design boundary explicit

section_contracts.title: Involved Items
checkitems: list the directly involved item
list the collaborating items only when they are necessary for understanding the design
section_contracts.expected_format:
This item design directly involves:

- `{ItemPath}`

This item design collaborates with:

- `{CollaboratorA}`
- `{CollaboratorB}`

section_contracts.title: Core Functions
checkitems: summarize the item design role
list the core functions only
explicitly state what is out of scope for this item design
section_contracts.expected_format:
`{ItemPath}` is the `{ItemRole}` item.

Its core functions are:

- `{CoreFunction1}`
- `{CoreFunction2}`
- `{CoreFunction3}`
- `{CoreFunction4}`

`{ItemName}` does not `{OutOfScope1}`, `{OutOfScope2}`, or `{OutOfScope3}`.

section_contracts.title: Core Classes
checkitems: this section must be expressed using UML class diagram language
do not replace the class diagram with prose-only description

section_contracts.title: Class Diagram
checkitems: show the important classes, interfaces, and dependencies
keep the diagram focused on core item structure

section_contracts.title: Core Class Responsibilities
checkitems: describe the role and responsibilities of the key classes or interfaces shown in the class diagram
keep one subsection per important class, interface, or component
do not restate every field unless it affects responsibilities or boundaries

section_contracts.title: Core Runtime Flow
checkitems: this section must be expressed using UML sequence diagram language
the diagram should focus on core runtime interactions between the item design and its collaborators

section_contracts.title: Main Sequence Diagram
checkitems: show the main runtime interaction between caller, item design, and collaborators
keep the flow focused on the primary success path

section_contracts.title: Core APIs And Fields
checkitems: define only stable interfaces and types needed to understand the item design
prefer concise and implementation-oriented type definitions

section_contracts.title: Public API
checkitems: define only the public API that upstream items need to call
keep the API structure stable and minimal
express the public API in a TypeScript code block
the public API may use interface, type, class signature, or other stable TypeScript boundary forms

section_contracts.title: Input Types
checkitems: define only input structures that belong to this item design
do not repeat upstream shared types unless this item design owns them
when the item design contains contract-style section definitions, prefer stable names such as `document_contracts` and `section_contracts`
input format must be defined explicitly in code blocks
do not use natural-language prose to describe input structure

section_contracts.title: Runtime Types
checkitems: define internal runtime structures only when they are necessary for understanding the design
when present, express runtime types in a TypeScript code block
runtime types may use interface, type, class, or other concise TypeScript structures
omit the entire subsection when the item design does not own meaningful runtime types
do not keep this subsection with prose-only not-applicable statements

section_contracts.title: Output Types
checkitems: define the stable output structure produced by this item design
make downstream-consumed fields explicit
output format must be defined explicitly in code blocks
do not use natural-language prose to describe output structure

section_contracts.title: Item-Specific Rules
checkitems: add this subsection only when the item design has important transformation, validation, mapping, or request-construction rules
express stable rules that downstream items depend on
prefer bullets over long prose

section_contracts.title: Constraints
checkitems: record the key item constraints and non-goals
include runtime semantics here when needed
avoid implementation trivia
